get.description:
Retrieve the current authenticated user's profile completion status.
Returns flags indicating which required fields are completed.

**Use Cases:**
- OAuth users who need to provide phone number and role
- Redirect logic after login (dashboard vs complete-profile page)
- Profile completion progress indicators
- Conditional UI rendering based on completion status

**Profile Requirements:**
- Phone number (phoneNo)
- Role assignment (student or owner)
- Both must be present for profileCompleted=true

**Auth Providers:**
- LOCAL: Profile auto-completed during signup
- GOOGLE: Profile incomplete, requires completion

**Response Fields:**
- `profileCompleted`: Overall completion status (boolean)
- `hasPhoneNo`: Whether phone number is set (boolean)
- `hasRole`: Whether role is assigned (boolean)
- `authProvider`: Authentication method (LOCAL/GOOGLE)

404.description: User not found in database

userNotFound.summary: User ID in token doesn't exist

post.description:
Complete user profile by providing phone number and role selection.
This endpoint is primarily for OAuth users (Google login) who don't provide
phone number and role during initial authentication.

**Profile Completion Flow:**
1. User logs in with Google OAuth
2. Backend creates user with profileCompleted=false
3. Frontend redirects to /complete-profile page
4. User provides phone number and selects role
5. Call this endpoint to complete profile
6. Backend updates user and creates Student/Owner profile
7. User can now access full application

**Profile Creation:**
- If role is "student": Creates Student profile with name, phoneNo
- If role is "owner": Creates Owner profile with name, phone
- Additional profile details can be added later via update endpoints

**Validation Rules:**
- Phone number: Minimum 10 digits, numbers only
- Role: Must be either "student" or "owner"
- Profile must not be already completed

**Role Options:**
- `student`: Users looking for hostels
- `owner`: Users managing/listing hostels

**Important:**
- Can only be called once per user
- Returns 400 if profile already completed
- Creates role if it doesn't exist in database
- After completion, user should be redirected to dashboard

phoneNo.description: User's phone number (minimum 10 digits, numbers only)

400.description: Invalid request or profile already completed

details.message: Phone number must be at least 10 digits

404.description: User not found

get.description:
Retrieve the authenticated user's complete profile including all related data.

**Use Cases:**
- Display user profile page
- Load user dashboard data
- Show user-specific navigation items based on role
- Display student or owner profile information
- List hostels owned by the user (for owners)

**Returned Data:**
- User basic info (id, name, email, phone, profile status)
- Role information (student or owner)
- Student profile (if role is student) - includes dob, gender, address
- Owner profile (if role is owner) - includes name, phone
- Hostels array (all hostels owned by the user)

**Profile Completeness:**
- If user has no student/owner profile: Returns null for both fields
- If user has no role: Returns null for role field
- If user has no hostels: Returns empty array []
- All edge cases are handled gracefully

**Authentication:**
- Requires valid JWT access token in Authorization header
- Returns current user's data based on token

patch.description:
Updates the caller's name, email, or phone number. Every field is
optional and only the supplied keys are written.

Two consequences of changing identity fields come back in the response
instead of having to be guessed:

- `phoneVerificationRequired` is true when the phone number changed. The
  account's verified flag is cleared, so the new number must be proven
  with `POST /users/profile/phone/verify` before it counts.
- `requiresReauthentication` is true when the email changed, because the
  old session's claims no longer describe the account.

An email or phone number already used by another account is rejected
with 409. When the caller has an owner profile, the name and phone are
mirrored onto it so the property listing never shows stale contact
details.

phoneVerificationRequired.description: True when the phone number changed and must be re-verified.

requiresReauthentication.description: True when the email changed and the session should be renewed.

404.description: No user matched the authenticated id

409.description: The email or phone number is already in use

`*Pending` counter under a row lock, so the last seat can genuinely only
be sold once.

post.summary: Create a stay hub counter booking (superadmin)
post.description:
Records a booking for a guest at a stay hub and confirms it immediately,
for an occupant who is settled in cash at the venue.

Because no payment is taken online, no gateway order is created and the
booking is born `confirmed` with `source: direct` and a null `paymentId`
— it is never left `pending`, which the abandoned-checkout sweep would
otherwise cancel. The seat is moved from the pending to the admitted
counter in a single transaction under a row lock, so the last seat
cannot be sold twice.

The occupant must be an existing guest account, identified by `guestId`
or by `occupantPhone`. `occupantPhone` is matched ignoring punctuation
and an optional leading country code, so `+91 98765 43210` finds a guest
stored as `9876543210`. A `stayhub_bookings` row cannot exist without a
guest, and the seat is later released against that guest's gender
bucket, so an unmatched number is a 404 rather than a placeholder
record. The guest's phone is not required to be OTP-verified: the
superadmin is vouching for the occupant at the counter.

The price is read from the stay hub's own `Rent` row for
`sharingType` and is never taken from the request, and the guest's
phone number is only used to identify them.

guestId.description: Known guest to book. Provide this or `occupantPhone`.

occupantPhone.description: Phone the guest registered with. Provide this or `guestId`.

byPhone.summary: Find the guest by the number they registered with

byGuestId.summary: Book a guest that is already known

guestNotified.description:
True when the occupant had an email address and a
confirmation was queued for them. False when the guest
registered by phone only, or the send failed — the
booking is still recorded either way.

Neither `guestId` nor `occupantPhone` was usable, or the guest's

delete.description:
Permanently removes a stay hub venue.

keys are not consistent about what a delete should mean — guests,
bookings and payments are `NO ACTION` / `RESTRICT` while rents and
files are `CASCADE` — so the dependants are counted first and the
response names them. A venue that still holds pricing rows or uploaded
photos is therefore never deleted silently alongside them.

post.summary: Save a hostel's whole room layout
post.description:
Replaces the hostel's room and bed layout in a single call, keyed by
`roomNumber`. Rooms present in the payload are created or updated, and
rooms that used to exist for this hostel but are absent from the payload
are removed together with their beds.

This is destructive by design: a floor-plan editor always submits the
complete plan, and a diff would let a stale tab silently drop rooms the
owner never removed.

a bed carrying an `id` is updated in place, a bed without an `id` is added
as `available`, and an existing bed missing from the list is removed —
except one that is `occupied` or `reserved`, which is always kept so a
live booking cannot be dropped by an edit. The caller must own the hostel
the room belongs to.

post.summary: Send a one-time code to a phone number
post.description:
Sends a six-digit code by SMS. `purpose` decides what the code may be
used for, and defaults to `login`.

With `purpose: login` the account is created when the number is unknown,
so signing up and signing in are the same request. The other purposes
require an existing account and do nothing if the number is not
registered.

In development, when SMS delivery is not configured, the code is
returned as `devCode` so a local client can complete the flow. That
field is absent in production — where an unconfigured SMS provider is
rejected up front with 503, leaving any already-sent code still valid
rather than silently replacing it with an undeliverable one.

Sending a code invalidates any unconsumed code previously issued for the
same number and purpose, so a client must use the newest one.

purpose.description: What the code may be used for.

devCode.description: Only present in development when SMS could not be delivered.

429.description: Still inside the resend cooldown; the message states the remaining seconds

503.description: Production has no SMS provider configured

post.description:
Verifies the six-digit code and, for `purpose: login`, signs the user in
by returning an access/refresh pair along with their user record and
owner profile if they have one.

Every other purpose only confirms the code was correct and returns
`verified: true` — the code becomes the proof that lets a separate step
proceed, such as `POST /users/profile/phone/verify`. This is why the
response shape depends on `purpose`.

A code is accepted at most `max_attempts` times and expires after the
configured window, and either outcome consumes the code rather than
locking the number — the client must request a fresh one.

owner.description: Only for `purpose: login`, and null when the account owns no property.

400.description: Payload failed validation, or the code was absent, expired, or incorrect.

404.description: The code was valid but no account exists for the number

429.description: The code's attempt allowance is used up

account, no payment, or simply prefers the desk. The booking is always
created as `direct` and unpaid, so there is no amount or payment id to
accept from the client.

`monthlyRentPaise` is still required explicitly rather than looked up:
the bed row's list price is the advertised rent, and a superadmin is
recording what was actually agreed for this walk-in.

**Notifying the guest**

Pass `occupantPhone` and the guest is emailed a booking confirmation.
The number is matched against registered accounts digit-for-digit, so
`+91 98765 43210` still finds an account stored as `9876543210`. The
booking is *not* linked to that guest's student profile, so it does not
appear in their app — only in the owner's occupancy and their inbox.

A number that matches no account is not an error: the walk-in is still
filed, and `guestNotified` comes back `false` so the console can show
that no mail went out. The property owner is emailed either way, since
the booking is not theirs.

confirmation. Matched ignoring punctuation and an optional
country code.

post.summary: Register a guest and send a verification code
post.description:
Creates a guest record and sends a six-digit code to their phone number.

No session is issued here. The response contains no token, because
registration must not be equivalent to authentication — the caller still
has to prove control of the number through `POST /auth/guest/verify-otp`.

`phoneNo` is the guest's identity credential, so it is required;
`email` stays optional for guests who do not have one. A venue is not
accepted: `guests.stayhubId` records where a guest is physically
allocated, and that is assigned by staff rather than self-selected.

phoneNo.description: Digits only, as dialled in the local format.

201.description: Guest registered and a code sent

post.summary: Verify a guest code and sign in
post.description:
Confirms a `guest_login` one-time code and issues the guest's first
session. The refresh token is also set as an httpOnly cookie, so a
browser client does not have to hold it in JavaScript.

The endpoint accepts the six-digit `code` rather than an emailed link,
and a wrong or expired code is refused without revealing which.

refreshToken.description: Also set as the `jwt` httpOnly cookie.

401.description: The code is wrong, expired, or no code was sent to this number

post.description:
Exchanges a refresh token for a new access/refresh pair.

The route is shared with the student and owner refresh flow: the service
branches on the token's principal type, so a single endpoint serves every
kind of session rather than three near-identical ones.

refreshToken.description: Falls back to the `jwt` cookie when omitted by a browser client.

401.description: The refresh token is invalid, expired, or revoked

post.description:
Clears the session cookie. This is the same handler as
`POST /auth/logout`, mounted on the guest prefix so a guest client has a
logout URL that matches the rest of its routes.

The call is safe to repeat: signing out twice, or without a session, is
not an error.

Emails a reset link when the address belongs to an account.

The response is identical whether or not the address exists. That is
deliberate: a different message for a known address would let anyone
enumerate which emails have accounts here.

message.example: If an account with that email exists, a password reset link has been sent.

post.summary: Reset a password with an emailed token
post.description:
Sets a new password using the token from the reset link and immediately
signs the user in, so a forgotten password does not also cost a login.
The new refresh token is set as an httpOnly cookie.

The new password must satisfy the account policy in full — at least 8
characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a
special character — and any one missing fails the request.

token.description: Single-use token from the reset link.

password.description: Must contain an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a special character.

400.description: The new password does not meet the account policy

401.description: The reset token is invalid or has expired
